raw_segments.text: Macbeth, aside. Two truths are told as happy prologues to the swelling act of the Imperial
I thank you, gentlemen. Aside. This supernatural soliciting cannot be ill, cannot be good.
If ill, why hath it given me earnest of success, commencing in a truth? I am Thane of Kador.
If good, why do I yield to that suggestion whose horrid image doth unfix my hair, and
make my seated heart knock at my ribs against the use of nature? Present fears are less
My thought, whose murder yet is but fantastical, shakes so my single state of man that function
is smothered in surmise, and nothing is but what is not.
